title: LiMeNEx: an interactive webserver on lipid biochemical gene-regulatory network.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Zenodo record's supplementary_data.zip (5.6 MB, CC-BY-4.0; 973 files) and parsed it. Table S3 (22 per-pathway CSVs) has 73,505 rows with columns TF, TargetGene, Tissue, Experiment, Chea, Signor, Trrust: 31,551 unique TF-gene pairs, 385 TFs, 324 target genes, 43 tissues. Table S4 has 452 literature pairs with Effect (184 Activation, 92 Repression, 176 Unknown). S2 lists 408 metabolites with ChEBI/KEGG/PubChem links. S7 holds the per-pathway node lists and CellDesigner XML files. No negative (non-interacting) pairs and no measured numeric outcome anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The edges are copied from SPP (Signaling Pathways Project) ChIP-seq, ChEA3, TRRUST v2 and SIGNOR 3.0, with manual literature checks; the confidence score is just a count of tissues per pair (1-3 tissues = low, 23,595 pairs). The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out; I used Zenodo instead. Webserver not probed.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo zip downloaded without login, CC-BY-4.0 (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No outcome column. The only possible target is whether a TF-to-gene link exists, but the files list only positive links, so the negatives would have to be built by sampling non-listed pairs (checked in S3/S4).

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are bare gene symbols. Sequences, promoter regions or expression features would all have to be fetched from outside sources (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable: categorical edges, no numeric values.

a5_enough_rows.note: 73,505 TF-gene-tissue rows, 31,551 unique pairs (counted). Only positives, though.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Roughly consistent: 324 target genes in S3 vs 330 enzymatic genes in the paper, 385 TFs vs 345 in the abstract. The gap is unexplained but small.

a8_label_provenance.note: The edges are copied from SPP ChIP-seq, ChEA3, TRRUST and SIGNOR, so a model would only re-learn those databases on a subset. The confidence score is computed from the tissue count, so it can't be used as a label.

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx (tissue gene expression), via gene symbol
integration.join_key: HGNC gene symbol (would need mapping to Ensembl IDs)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not pursued: the regulatory edges already come from larger public resources (SPP, ChEA3), so joining this subset adds nothing those sources don't already have.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained here could only claim to reproduce which ChIP-seq or literature TF-to-gene links the source databases list for 324 human lipid-metabolism genes. It could not claim to find true regulation, because non-links were never tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a transcription factor and a lipid-enzyme gene to predict whether the factor regulates that gene, and in which tissues.
plain_idea.train_on: Pairs of a gene-controlling protein (transcription factor) and a lipid-enzyme gene, 31,551 unique positive pairs across 43 tissues (counted). No confirmed non-pairs.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a link exists. The 'true' answers are entries copied from public ChIP-seq (protein-DNA binding experiment) and literature databases, not new measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Lipid biologists could rank candidate regulators of an enzyme. But the source databases already do this at genome scale, so a subset model would teach little.

ml_idea: Link prediction on a TF-to-enzyme-gene graph with tissue context. Rejected: positive-only edges copied from existing databases, inputs are bare gene symbols, and the larger upstream sources (SPP, ChEA3) are the better place to do this.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the unzipped file sizes; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count how many rows record a tested non-interaction. Done: zero, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A3 and A8. The files hold only positive TF-to-gene links copied from SPP, ChEA3, TRRUST and SIGNOR, keyed by gene symbol. There is no measured outcome and no negatives, and any label would just redistribute existing databases.
